diff: The World Swing Dance Council (WSDC) is a non-profit organization focused on promoting and growing West Coast
(WCS) dance at the global level. Its mission is “To inspire a global passion for
and guide community growth through supporting events, dancers, and competitors with fairness, integrity, and respect.”
The WSDC respects the interests of both new and existing members of the entire West Coast
dance community. As a governing body of WSDC Registry Events (“Registry Events”), the WSDC Board of Directors (“Board”) has developed these Registry Event rules to ensure integrity,

Registry Events are swing dance events organized and hosted by Professional Members (“Members”) of the WSDC and approved by its Board. Registry Events must meet standards set by the WSDC Board, demonstrating integrity and the highest ethical standards; sufficient event size, scope, and structure; and financial viability and stability. Registry Events offer a mix of social dancing,
and competition, bringing together local, regional, national and international dancers.

IV. Guideline Procedure – Exception to Randomization Rule.
In some circumstances, an Event may encounter a conflict between two rules:
Member Events must publish a Code of Conduct with clear reporting and implementation plans. [See Section 1.2.5 .]
All WSDC Jack and Jill contests must maintain the integrity of random and unbiased selection [See Section 3.4.9 .]
In case of such a conflict, Events may narrowly depart from strict randomization in order to prevent two individuals from being paired together.

The following options are all considered best practices. Chief Judges and Event Directors should work together to decide ahead of time which is the right approach for the Event. The WSDC supports any of these approaches.

Events should document in advance the specific conditions under which Code of Conduct obligations will take precedence over randomization, and which process or options will be used. Departures from randomization should occur only in extreme circumstances when true randomization cannot be maintained. The privacy of all parties must be protected throughout.
Prelims/Semis
The Chief Judge (CJ) may assign competitors with a conflict into separate heats or prevent specific pairings, when warranted by the Code of Conduct and its implementation plan.
Finals

Option 1 “On the floor” Pairings: Randomization may not be compromised in any way. Competitors have the option to withdraw from the contest. Contest proceeds with remaining competitors. [Randomization maintained.]

Option 2 Advance Pairings: Competitor A confirms with the CJ that they choose to withdraw from finals automatically if they draw Competitor B. CJ directs the scorekeeper to randomize all pairings in advance, eliminating the on-floor partner draw. If the affected competitors are paired by the system, Competitor A is withdrawn and replaced with an alternate. All competitor pairings are re-drawn. [Randomization maintained.]

Option 3: Advance Pairings: The CJ reviews all pairing reports before the contest begins. If competitors with a conflict draw one another, CJ directs the scorekeeper to re-draw competitor pairings. [Randomization compromised; Incident report must be filed to notify WSDC of rule violation, documentation, and justification.]
V. Best Practices and Guidelines for Chief Judges from the Chief Judge Committee
Guideline Procedures for Self-Judging WSDC Jack & Jill Champion & All Invitationals - Finals
Prelims/Semis/Quarters
Cannot be self-judged.
Finals
May be self-judged.
The role with the most competitors must self-judge.
If both roles are even, you may choose a role by random selection (toss a coin, have audience participation, draw a number, etc.).
If there are fewer than ten (10) couples, both sides should judge for a better data point, but that will depend on the number of tablets available.
You cannot use an even number of judges for relative placement. You must use an odd number of judges for relative placement. [See 3.4.8c .]
If there is an even number of competitors, the chief judge will assign another judge to bring the total to an odd number.
Tablets/Paper Scoring
If the Chief Judge wants to prevent competitors from knowing who their partner will be:
The CJ may request that the scorer use the tablet system to either randomize on the spot or in advance, showing only one couple at a time (e.g., Scoring.dance, and Event Express Pro).
If the tablet system cannot randomize competitors on the spot or hide competitors' pairings, the CJ may use paper scoring if they choose.

If paper scoring is used, the Chief Judge or Secondary Chief Judge is responsible for auditing the contest and ensuring that when the scores are entered into the tablet system, the bib numbers, names, and scores are correct.
